request.state: Verified constraints for a draft DSL decision: actual Mail policy grants an authenticated eligible recipient service/recipient/kind/state/notice_state/completed/created. Its notification association is absent from that grant. Actual declaration computes notice_state:DeliveryResult.status? from row.notification?.status, so the rule requiring readable dependencies blocks it. Eligibility means the current verified contact is linked to the caller and the customer/contact remain active and unarchived; staff additionally has its own full-row policy constrained by workplace access. Policies add their permitted fields together, with ordinary derivations evaluated in viewer mode. Field selectors parse as paths but value-member grants have no defined semantics. A delivery(Mail.send)? contains id, status, result and error under containing-field authorization and further retention/result/error checks. Current draft JS calls delivery(c,handle); authorization provenance for a leaf-only read has not been established. Receipt observations join the owner transaction fence without a business-row write. The application needs recipient status/no-request presentation while hiding the attempt identity, provider result, safe error and frozen message; revoked access must stop all such presentation. Staff retains its existing detail. The current-ID completion handler continues to perform only received-to-notified on succeeded/non-null result. Collection and other domain decisions stay separate. Existing privileged read scenarios can return explicitly granted typed results; existing callbacks can store a separately granted status field. Nothing is implemented and there is no measured performance or token result. Consider each complete route without treating existing draft syntax as a compatibility obligation. Preserve dependency-based confidentiality, genuine null semantics and absence of global receipt lookup.

disclosure.instructions: Which route provides the strongest overall fit to the verified constraints and required recipient experience?

criteria.leaf_grants: Authorize named value leaves with current selector syntax, for example notification.status, only within embedded schemas and associated receipts. Allow the path null test required for optional projection, deny its siblings/container/identity, and require separate permission for the derived result. A target lookup must carry record/path origin and enforce exact requested leaves, serialization and the receipt read fence. This avoids status copies while introducing defined nested-value permission behavior.
criteria.authority_read: Publish a typed scope=authority status query with authenticated by and explicit live recipient/staff eligibility checks on the Item. Its result grants only the optional status; display it using the existing read-form result and reuse the query in MCP. Whole-field permission rules remain as written. The tradeoff is an added operation/schema and presentation invocation instead of the original computed table cell.
criteria.status_mirror: Maintain a stored summary under its existing independent grant. Enqueue records pending, then a current-attempt-matched completion copies the status while retaining the separate successful received-to-notified rule. No nested-value permission extension or new read operation is needed. The app retains repeated receipt bookkeeping, callback-lagged presentation and domain history/version changes caused by copied transport updates.
